source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including all written/read and other notes, not normalized reconstructions.
source.public_versification_note: Public Joshua 18–24 and Hebrew source references align one to one. All 216 original source records are bound exactly once.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keep assembly, sacred tent and conquest claim together at the new location.
verses.before: The whole congregation of the children of Israel assembled at Shiloh and set up the tent of meeting there. The land was subdued before them.
verses.after: The whole assembly of Israel gathered at Shiloh and set up the tent of meeting there. The land had been subdued before them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The whole congregation of the children of Israel assembled at Shiloh and set up the tent of meeting there. The land was subdued before them.

verses.rationale: Make the unfinished allocation clear while retaining the exact seven tribes.
verses.before: Seven tribes remained among the children of Israel that had not yet divided their inheritance.
verses.after: But seven tribes of Israel still had not received their allotted inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: Seven tribes remained among the children of Israel that had not yet divided their inheritance.

verses.rationale: Turn the rebuke into natural speech without removing the contrast between gift and action.
verses.before: Joshua said to the children of Israel, “How long will you be slack about going in to possess the land that the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has given you?
verses.after: Joshua said to the Israelites, “How long will you put off going in to possess the land the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has given you?
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua said to the children of Israel, “How long will you be slack about going in to possess the land that the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has given you?

verses.rationale: Retain three men per tribe and all stages of surveying, writing and return.
verses.before: Provide three men from each tribe, and I will send them. They will arise and walk through the land, write a description of it according to their inheritance, and come to me.
verses.after: Choose three men from each tribe. I will send them out to travel through the land, write a description of it for the inheritance, and return to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Provide three men from each tribe, and I will send them. They shall arise and walk through the land, write a description of it according to their inheritance, and come to me.

verses.rationale: Preserve the seven shares alongside the two established territories.
verses.before: They will divide it into seven portions. Judah will remain in its territory on the south, and the house of Joseph will remain in their territory on the north.
verses.after: They are to divide it into seven parts. Judah will remain in its territory to the south, and Joseph’s household in its territory to the north.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall divide it into seven portions. Judah shall remain in its territory on the south, and the house of Joseph shall remain in their territory on the north.

verses.rationale: Keep the repeated written survey, seven parts and divine presence in the allocation.
verses.before: You will describe the land in seven portions and bring the description here to me. Then I will cast lots for you here before the LORD our God.
verses.after: Write a description of the land in seven parts and bring it here to me. I will cast lots for you here before the LORD our God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall describe the land in seven portions and bring the description here to me. Then I will cast lots for you here before the LORD our God.

verses.rationale: Retain priestly service as Levi’s inheritance here and all three eastern recipients.
verses.before: For the Levites have no portion among you, because the priesthood of the LORD is their inheritance. Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan toward the east, which Moses servant of the LORD gave them.”
verses.after: The Levites have no share among you, because the priestly service of the LORD is their inheritance. Gad, Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh have already received their inheritance east of the Jordan, given to them by Moses, the LORD’s servant.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For the Levites have no portion among you, because the priesthood of the LORD is their inheritance. Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan toward the east, which Moses servant of the LORD gave them.”

verses.rationale: Unfold the departure and instruction without suppressing its repeated actions and setting.
verses.before: The men arose and went. Joshua commanded people who went to describe the land, saying, “Go, walk through the land, describe it, and return to me. Then I will cast lots for you here before the LORD at Shiloh.”
verses.after: The men got ready to leave. Joshua instructed those going to describe the land: “Go through the land and write a description of it. Then return to me, and I will cast lots for you here at Shiloh before the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The men arose and went. Joshua commanded those who went to describe the land, saying, “Go, walk through the land, describe it, and return to me. Then I will cast lots for you here before the LORD at Shiloh.”

verses.rationale: Keep the written medium, town-based survey, seven divisions and return.
verses.before: The men went, passed through the land, and described it by cities in seven portions in a scroll. Then they came to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.
verses.after: The men traveled through the land and wrote a description on a scroll, town by town, in seven parts. Then they returned to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh.
verses.tsw_comparator: The men went, passed through the land, and described it by cities in seven portions in a scroll. Then they came to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.

verses.rationale: Retain allocation before the LORD as distinct from surveying or possession.
verses.before: Joshua cast lots for them at Shiloh before the LORD, and there Joshua divided the land to the children of Israel according to their divisions.
verses.after: Joshua cast lots for them at Shiloh before the LORD. There he divided the land among the Israelites, giving each its share.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua cast lots for them at Shiloh before the LORD, and there Joshua divided the land to the children of Israel according to their divisions.

verses.rationale: Identify the two neighboring groups while keeping Benjamin’s clan structure.
verses.before: The lot of the tribe of the children of Benjamin came up according to their clans. The territory of their lot went out between the children of Judah and the children of Joseph.
verses.after: The lot for Benjamin’s clans came up. Their allotted territory lay between Judah’s descendants and Joseph’s descendants.
verses.tsw_comparator: The lot of the tribe of the children of Benjamin came up according to their clans. The territory of their lot went out between the children of Judah and the children of Joseph.

verses.rationale: Keep all directional stages; the written/read agreement difference does not alter the English endpoint.
verses.before: Their border on the north side began at the Jordan. The border went up to the north shoulder of Jericho, went up through the hill country westward, and ended at the wilderness of Beth-Aven.
verses.after: Their northern boundary began at the Jordan, climbed the northern flank of Jericho, went west into the hills, and ended at the wilderness of Beth-aven.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their border on the north side began at the Jordan. The border went up to the north shoulder of Jericho, went up through the hill country westward, and ended at the wilderness of Beth-Aven.

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated Luz and explicit Bethel identification, unlike the preceding chapter’s separate boundary names.
verses.before: From there the border crossed to Luz, to the south shoulder of Luz—that is, Bethel—and the border went down to Ataroth-Addar, by the mountain south of Lower Beth-Horon.
verses.after: From there it passed to Luz, along the southern flank of Luz, that is, Bethel. It descended to Ataroth-addar, on the hill south of Lower Beth-horon.
verses.tsw_comparator: From there the border crossed to Luz, to the south shoulder of Luz—that is, Bethel—and the border went down to Ataroth-Addar, by the mountain south of Lower Beth-Horon.

verses.rationale: Render sea-side as west, preserving the repeated southern qualifiers without making the Mediterranean this tribe’s boundary.
verses.before: The border turned and curved on the western side southward from the mountain that is before Beth-Horon on the south, and it ended at Kiriath-Baal—that is, Kiriath-Jearim—a city of the children of Judah. This was the western side.
verses.after: On the western side, the boundary curved and turned south from the hill facing Beth-horon on the south. It ended at Kiriath-baal, that is, Kiriath-jearim, a town of Judah. This was the western side.
verses.tsw_comparator: The border turned and curved on the western side southward from the mountain that is before Beth-Horon on the south, and it ended at Kiriath-Baal—that is, Kiriath-Jearim—a city of the children of Judah. This was the western side.

verses.rationale: Retain the source’s difficult westward direction rather than replacing it with a geographically easier eastward reading.
verses.before: The southern side began at the edge of Kiriath-Jearim. The border went out westward and went out to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.
verses.after: The southern side began at the edge of Kiriath-jearim. The boundary went west and reached the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The southern side began at the edge of Kiriath-Jearim. The border went out westward and went out to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.

verses.rationale: Unfold the successive descents and preserve both valleys and directional relationships.
verses.before: The border went down to the edge of the mountain that is before the Valley of Ben-Hinnom, which is in the Valley of Rephaim northward. It went down the Valley of Hinnom to the south shoulder of the Jebusite and down to En-Rogel.
verses.after: It descended to the edge of the hill facing the Valley of Ben-hinnom, at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim. It went down the Valley of Hinnom, along the southern flank of the Jebusites, and down to En-rogel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The border went down to the edge of the mountain that is before the Valley of Ben-Hinnom, which is in the Valley of Rephaim northward. It went down the Valley of Hinnom to the south shoulder of the Jebusite and down to En-Rogel.

verses.rationale: Keep Geliloth as written here rather than substituting Gilgal from the parallel boundary description.
verses.before: It curved northward and went out to En-Shemesh, went out to Geliloth, which is opposite the ascent of Adummim, and went down to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
verses.after: It curved north, reached En-shemesh, and continued to Geliloth, opposite the Ascent of Adummim. Then it descended to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
verses.tsw_comparator: It curved northward and went out to En-Shemesh, went out to Geliloth, which is opposite the ascent of Adummim, and went down to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.

verses.rationale: Retain the plain reference without supplying Beth-arabah from another boundary text.
verses.before: It crossed to the shoulder opposite the Arabah northward and went down to the Arabah.
verses.after: It passed along the northern flank facing the Arabah and descended into the Arabah.
verses.tsw_comparator: It crossed to the shoulder opposite the Arabah northward and went down to the Arabah.

verses.rationale: Keep the tongue image and distinguish northern sea projection from southern river endpoint.
verses.before: The border crossed to the north shoulder of Beth-Hoglah, and the border ended at the northern bay of the Salt Sea, at the southern end of the Jordan. This was the southern border.
verses.after: The boundary passed the northern flank of Beth-hoglah and ended at the northern tongue of the Salt Sea, at the southern end of the Jordan. This was the southern boundary.
verses.tsw_comparator: The border crossed to the north shoulder of Beth-Hoglah, and the border ended at the northern bay of the Salt Sea, at the southern end of the Jordan. This was the southern border.

verses.rationale: Close the full circuit and retain the clan allocation.
verses.before: The Jordan bordered it on the eastern side. This was the inheritance of the children of Benjamin according to its borders all around, according to their clans.
verses.after: The Jordan formed the eastern boundary. This was Benjamin’s inheritance, with its surrounding boundaries, clan by clan.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Jordan bordered it on the eastern side. This was the inheritance of the children of Benjamin according to its borders all around, according to their clans.

verses.after: The towns of Benjamin’s clans were Jericho, Beth-hoglah, Emek-keziz,
verses.tsw_comparator: The cities of the tribe of the children of Benjamin according to their clans were Jericho, Beth-Hoglah, Emek-Keziz,

verses.after: Chephar-ammonah, Ophni, and Geba—twelve towns, with their villages.

verses.after: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth,

verses.rationale: Keep the source’s three town names and order.

verses.after: Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah,

verses.rationale: Preserve each entry in the continuing list.

verses.after: Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah,

verses.rationale: Read Gibeath and Kiriath as separate entries while noting compressed naming; preserve Jerusalem and the stated total.

verses.after: Zela, Haeleph, the Jebusite town, that is, Jerusalem, Gibeath, and Kiriath—fourteen towns, with their villages. This was Benjamin’s inheritance, clan by clan.
verses.tsw_comparator: Zelah, Haeleph, the Jebusite—that is, Jerusalem—Gibeah, and Kiriath: fourteen cities with their villages. This was the inheritance of the children of Benjamin according to their clans.

verses.rationale: Retain lot order and the unusual inheritance within another tribe’s allotment.
verses.before: The second lot came out for Simeon, for the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their clans. Their inheritance was within the inheritance of the children of Judah.
verses.after: The second lot came out for Simeon’s clans. Their inheritance lay within Judah’s inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: The second lot came out for Simeon, for the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their clans. Their inheritance was within the inheritance of the children of Judah.

verses.rationale: Keep both Beer-sheba and Sheba rather than deleting the second name to reconcile the later total.
verses.before: They had in their inheritance Beersheba, Sheba, Moladah,
verses.after: Their inheritance included Beer-sheba, Sheba, Moladah,
verses.tsw_comparator: They had in their inheritance Beersheba, Sheba, Moladah,

verses.rationale: Retain Balah as this passage’s form and preserve all three names.
verses.before: Hazar-Shual, Balah, Ezem,
verses.after: Hazar-shual, Balah, Ezem,
verses.tsw_comparator: Hazar-Shual, Balah, Ezem,

verses.rationale: Keep Bethul without harmonizing another list’s name.
verses.before: Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah,
verses.after: Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah,
verses.tsw_comparator: Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah,

verses.rationale: Preserve the three towns in source order.
verses.before: Ziklag, Beth-Marcaboth, Hazar-Susah,
verses.after: Ziklag, Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susah,
verses.tsw_comparator: Ziklag, Beth-Marcaboth, Hazar-Susah,

verses.rationale: Retain stated thirteen alongside the fourteen listed names and continue into the next group.
verses.before: Beth-Lebaoth, and Sharuhen: thirteen cities with their villages;
verses.after: Beth-lebaoth, and Sharuhen—thirteen towns, with their villages;
verses.tsw_comparator: Beth-Lebaoth, and Sharuhen: thirteen cities with their villages;

verses.rationale: Keep Ain and Rimmon distinct to match the stated four-town group.
verses.before: Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan: four cities with their villages;
verses.after: Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan—four towns, with their villages;
verses.tsw_comparator: Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan: four cities with their villages;

verses.rationale: Retain the compressed Baalath-beer and Ramath naming without inventing a second boundary span.
verses.before: and all the villages that were around these cities as far as Baalath-Beer, Ramah of the Negev. This was the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their clans.
verses.after: and all the villages around these towns as far as Baalath-beer, Ramath of the Negev. This was the inheritance of the tribe of Simeon, clan by clan.
verses.tsw_comparator: and all the villages that were around these cities as far as Baalath-Beer, Ramah of the Negev. This was the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their clans.

verses.rationale: Preserve the stated practical reason and repeated internal allotment.
verses.before: The inheritance of the children of Simeon was taken from the portion of the children of Judah, for the portion of the children of Judah was too large for them. So the children of Simeon received an inheritance within their inheritance.
verses.after: Simeon’s inheritance came from Judah’s portion, because Judah’s share was too large for them. So Simeon’s descendants received an inheritance within Judah’s.
verses.tsw_comparator: The inheritance of the children of Simeon was taken from the portion of the children of Judah, for the portion of the children of Judah was too large for them. So the children of Simeon received an inheritance within their inheritance.

verses.rationale: Keep third-lot order and the boundary’s starting reference.
verses.before: The third lot came up for the children of Zebulun according to their clans. The border of their inheritance extended as far as Sarid.
verses.after: The third lot came up for Zebulun’s clans. The boundary of their inheritance reached Sarid.
verses.tsw_comparator: The third lot came up for the children of Zebulun according to their clans. The border of their inheritance extended as far as Sarid.

verses.rationale: Preserve the ascent, westward direction and every waypoint.
verses.before: Their border went up westward to Maralah, reached Dabbesheth, and reached the wadi that is before Jokneam.
verses.after: Their boundary went up westward to Maralah, reached Dabbesheth, and reached the wadi opposite Jokneam.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their border went up westward to Maralah, reached Dabbesheth, and reached the wadi that is before Jokneam.

verses.rationale: Keep the repeated east/sunrise orientation and the two subsequent places.
verses.before: It turned from Sarid eastward toward the sunrise, to the border of Chisloth-Tabor, went out to Daberath, and went up to Japhia.
verses.after: From Sarid it turned east, toward the sunrise, to the territory of Chisloth-tabor. It continued to Daberath and went up to Japhia.
verses.tsw_comparator: It turned from Sarid eastward toward the sunrise, to the border of Chisloth-Tabor, went out to Daberath, and went up to Japhia.

verses.rationale: Retain each name and render the difficult intervening form as a boundary curve rather than silently inventing a town.
verses.before: From there it crossed eastward toward the sunrise to Gath-Hepher, to Eth-Kazin, went out at Rimmon, and curved toward Neah.
verses.after: From there it passed eastward to Gath-hepher and Eth-kazin, and continued to Rimmon, curving toward Neah.
verses.tsw_comparator: From there it crossed eastward toward the sunrise to Gath-Hepher, to Eth-Kazin, went out at Rimmon, and curved toward Neah.

verses.rationale: Keep northern curve and valley endpoint distinct.
verses.before: The border went around it on the north to Hannathon, and it ended at the Valley of Iphtah-El.
verses.after: The boundary curved around on the north to Hannathon and ended at the Valley of Iphtah-el.
verses.tsw_comparator: The border went around it on the north to Hannathon, and it ended at the Valley of Iphtah-El.

verses.rationale: Retain the five names and stated twelve without supplying missing towns or assuming this Bethlehem is Judah’s.
verses.before: Also Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem: twelve cities with their villages.
verses.after: It included Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem—twelve towns, with their villages.
verses.tsw_comparator: Also Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem: twelve cities with their villages.

verses.rationale: Make the closing formula natural while preserving villages and clans.
verses.before: This was the inheritance of the children of Zebulun according to their clans, these cities with their villages.
verses.after: These towns and their villages were the inheritance of Zebulun’s descendants, clan by clan.
verses.tsw_comparator: This was the inheritance of the children of Zebulun according to their clans, these cities with their villages.

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated tribal identification and fourth-lot sequence.
verses.before: The fourth lot came out for Issachar, for the children of Issachar according to their clans.
verses.after: The fourth lot came out for Issachar, for Issachar’s descendants by their clans.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fourth lot came out for Issachar, for the children of Issachar according to their clans.

verses.after: Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath,

verses.after: Rabbith, Kishion, Ebez,

verses.rationale: Retain four separate entries before the boundary resumes.
verses.before: Remeth, En-Gannim, En-Haddah, and Beth-Pazzez.
verses.after: Remeth, En-gannim, En-haddah, and Beth-pazzez.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remeth, En-Gannim, En-Haddah, and Beth-Pazzez.

verses.rationale: Follow the reading-tradition name and preserve all three places, river and total.
verses.before: The border reached Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth-Shemesh, and their border ended at the Jordan: sixteen cities with their villages.
verses.after: The boundary reached Tabor, Shahazimah, and Beth-shemesh, and ended at the Jordan—sixteen towns, with their villages.
verses.tsw_comparator: The border reached Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth-Shemesh, and their border ended at the Jordan: sixteen cities with their villages.

verses.rationale: Keep tribe, clans and settlement types in the closing formula.
verses.before: This was the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Issachar according to their clans, the cities with their villages.
verses.after: These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the tribe of Issachar, clan by clan.
verses.tsw_comparator: This was the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Issachar according to their clans, the cities with their villages.

verses.rationale: Retain fifth-lot order and clan-based allocation.

verses.after: The fifth lot came out for the tribe of Asher, clan by clan.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fifth lot came out for the tribe of the children of Asher according to their clans.

verses.rationale: Keep all leadership categories and repeat Joshua’s age in his own voice. Consistency refinement: Uses officers for shoterim, matching 1:10, 3:2 and 8:33 so readers recognize the same community role at the farewell assembly; all four leadership categories remain.
verses.before: Joshua called all Israel, their elders, heads, judges, and officers, and said to them, “I am old, advanced in days.
verses.after: He summoned all Israel—its elders, heads, judges, and officers—and told them, “I am old, advanced in years.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua called all Israel, their elders, heads, judges, and officers, and said to them, “I am old, advanced in days.

consistency_history.prior_after: He summoned all Israel—its elders, heads, judges, and officials—and told them, “I am old, advanced in years.

consistency_history.rationale: Uses officers for shoterim, matching 1:10, 3:2 and 8:33 so readers recognize the same community role at the farewell assembly; all four leadership categories remain.

verses.rationale: Preserve eyewitness appeal, all nations and explicit divine military agency.
verses.before: You have seen all that the LORD your God has done to all these nations before you, for the LORD your God is the one who fought for you.
verses.after: You have seen everything the LORD your God has done to all these nations before you. It is the LORD your God who has fought for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have seen all that the LORD your God has done to all these nations before you, for the LORD your God is the one who fought for you.

verses.rationale: Keep remaining nations and destroyed nations together within the allotted span rather than rewriting all as conquered land.
verses.before: See, I have allotted to you as an inheritance for your tribes these nations that remain, along with all the nations that I have cut off, from the Jordan to the Great Sea toward the setting of the sun.
verses.after: Look, I have allotted these remaining nations to your tribes as an inheritance, together with all the nations I cut off, from the Jordan to the Great Sea toward the sunset.
verses.tsw_comparator: See, I have allotted to you as an inheritance for your tribes these nations that remain, along with all the nations that I have cut off, from the Jordan to the Great Sea toward the setting of the sun.

verses.rationale: Retain two expulsion verbs and future possession alongside earlier completion summaries.
verses.before: The LORD your God himself will push them out from before you and drive them out from before you, and you will possess their land, as the LORD your God spoke to you.
verses.after: The LORD your God himself will push them back and drive them out before you. You will take possession of their land, as the LORD your God promised you.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD your God himself will push them out from before you and drive them out from before you, and you shall possess their land, as the LORD your God spoke to you.

verses.rationale: Link strength, written instruction and right/left imagery with the opening commission.
verses.before: So be very strong to keep and do all that is written in the book of the instruction of Moses, not turning aside from it to the right or to the left,
verses.after: Be very strong in keeping and carrying out everything written in the scroll of Moses’ instruction. Do not turn from it to the right or the left.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore be very strong to keep and do all that is written in the book of the instruction of Moses, not turning aside from it to the right or to the left,

verses.rationale: Preserve the prohibitions and the causative oath expression rather than collapsing the sequence into generic worship.
verses.before: so that you do not mix with these nations that remain among you or make mention of the names of their gods, cause anyone to swear by them, serve them, or bow down to them.
verses.after: Do not join these nations that remain among you. Do not invoke the names of their gods, have oaths sworn by them, serve them, or bow down to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that you do not mix with these nations that remain among you or make mention of the names of their gods, cause anyone to swear by them, serve them, or bow down to them.

verses.rationale: Keep the attachment image and Joshua’s positive retrospective claim.
verses.before: But you will cling to the LORD your God, as you have done to this day.
verses.after: Cling to the LORD your God, as you have done to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you shall cling to the LORD your God, as you have done to this day.

verses.rationale: Retain the comprehensive claim without explaining away earlier defeats.
verses.before: For the LORD has driven out from before you great and strong nations, and as for you, no one has stood before you to this day.
verses.after: The LORD has driven out great and powerful nations before you. As for you, no one has stood against you to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD has driven out from before you great and strong nations, and as for you, no one has stood before you to this day.

verses.rationale: Keep one-to-thousand contrast, specific warrior context and divine agency.
verses.before: One man from you has pursued a thousand, for the LORD your God is the one who fights for you, as he spoke to you.
verses.after: One of your men puts a thousand to flight, because the LORD your God fights for you, as he promised.
verses.tsw_comparator: One man from you has pursued a thousand, for the LORD your God is the one who fights for you, as he spoke to you.

verses.rationale: Retain care for their lives and love as the concrete command.
verses.before: So be very careful for your own lives to love the LORD your God.
verses.after: Take great care, for your own lives, to love the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: So be very careful for your own lives to love the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Keep intermarriage and reciprocal association explicit and contrast clinging to nations with clinging to the LORD.
verses.before: For if you turn back and cling to the remnant of these nations, these that remain with you, and intermarry with them, and go in to them and they to you,
verses.after: But if you turn back and cling to the rest of these nations still among you, intermarry with them, and associate with them as they do with you,
verses.tsw_comparator: For if you turn back and cling to the remnant of these nations, these that remain with you, and intermarry with them, and go in to them and they to you,

verses.rationale: Retain the full sequence of bodily harm images, cessation of expulsion and threatened loss of the gift.
verses.before: know for certain that the LORD your God will no longer drive out these nations from before you. They will become a snare and a trap for you, a whip on your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good land that the LORD your God has given you.
verses.after: know for certain that the LORD your God will no longer drive these nations out before you. They will become a trap and a snare for you, whips against your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good ground the LORD your God has given you.
verses.tsw_comparator: know for certain that the LORD your God will no longer drive out these nations from before you. They shall become a snare and a trap for you, a whip on your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good land that the LORD your God has given you.

verses.rationale: Keep death idiom, heart/being and repeated total fulfillment rather than shortening away the emphasis.
verses.before: Look, today I am going the way of all the earth. You know with all your heart and with all your life that not one word has failed from all the good words that the LORD your God spoke concerning you. All have come to pass for you; not one word of them has failed.
verses.after: Today I am going the way of all the earth. You know with all your heart and all your being that not one word has failed of all the good the LORD your God promised you. It has all come to pass for you; not one word has failed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, today I am going the way of all the earth. You know with all your heart and with all your life that not one word has failed from all the good words that the LORD your God spoke concerning you. All have come to pass for you; not one word of them has failed.

verses.rationale: Preserve the good/harm correspondence and explicit divine destruction without replacing it with mere natural consequences.
verses.before: And just as every good word that the LORD your God spoke to you has come upon you, so the LORD will bring upon you every harmful word until he destroys you from this good land that the LORD your God has given you,
verses.after: Just as all the good the LORD your God promised has come upon you, so the LORD will bring all the harm upon you, until he destroys you from this good ground he has given you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And just as every good word that the LORD your God spoke to you has come upon you, so the LORD will bring upon you every harmful word until he destroys you from this good land that the LORD your God has given you,

verses.rationale: Keep covenant violation, other-god service, divine anger and rapid loss together in the conditional warning.
verses.before: if you transgress the covenant of the LORD your God that he commanded you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them. Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and you will quickly perish from the good land that he has given you.”
verses.after: If you violate the covenant the LORD your God commanded you to keep, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them, the LORD’s anger will burn against you. You will quickly perish from the good land he has given you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: if you transgress the covenant of the LORD your God that he commanded you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them. Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and you will quickly perish from the good land that he has given you.”

verses.rationale: Preserve all groups, Shechem and the formal divine presence. Consistency refinement: Keeps the same officers designation for shoterim as in the earlier assemblies and 23:2, preserving Shechem, the four leadership categories and presentation before God.
verses.before: Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem and summoned the elders of Israel, its heads, its judges, and its officers, and they presented themselves before God.
verses.after: Joshua gathered all Israel’s tribes at Shechem. He summoned Israel’s elders, heads, judges, and officers, and they presented themselves before God.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem and summoned the elders of Israel, its heads, its judges, and its officers, and they presented themselves before God.

consistency_history.prior_after: Joshua gathered all Israel’s tribes at Shechem. He summoned Israel’s elders, heads, judges, and officials, and they presented themselves before God.
consistency_history.prior_rationale: Preserve all groups, Shechem and the formal divine presence.
consistency_history.rationale: Keeps the same officers designation for shoterim as in the earlier assemblies and 23:2, preserving Shechem, the four leadership categories and presentation before God.

verses.rationale: Retain ancestors’ other-god service and the opening of a divine first-person historical speech; explain River selectively.
verses.before: Joshua said to all the people, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Long ago your fathers lived beyond the River—Terah, the father of Abraham and of Nahor—and they served other gods.
verses.after: Joshua told all the people, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Long ago your ancestors lived beyond the River, including Terah, the father of Abraham and Nahor. They served other gods.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Joshua said to all the people, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Long ago your fathers lived beyond the River—Terah, the father of Abraham and of Nahor—and they served other gods.

verses.rationale: Keep divine initiative, full land scope, offspring and the specific gift of Isaac.
verses.before: Then I took your father Abraham from beyond the River and led him through all the land of Canaan and made his offspring many. I gave him Isaac.
verses.after: I took your ancestor Abraham from beyond the River and led him through all the land of Canaan. I multiplied his offspring and gave him Isaac.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I took your father Abraham from beyond the River and led him through all the land of Canaan and made his offspring many. I gave him Isaac.

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated divine gifts and distinction between Esau’s land and Jacob’s descent.
verses.before: “And to Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. To Esau I gave Mount Seir to possess, but Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
verses.after: To Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Seir to possess, while Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And to Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. To Esau I gave Mount Seir to possess, but Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retain both messengers and the unspecific description of the acts rather than importing a list of plagues.
verses.before: Then I sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt according to what I did in its midst, and afterward I brought you out.
verses.after: I sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt with what I did in its midst. After that I brought you out.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt according to what I did in its midst, and afterward I brought you out.

verses.rationale: Keep shifts between ancestors and you, full military equipment and Hebrew sea designation.
verses.before: I brought your fathers out from Egypt, and you came to the sea. The Egyptians pursued your fathers with chariots and horsemen to the Sea of Reeds.
verses.after: I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, and you came to the sea. The Egyptians pursued your ancestors with chariots and horsemen to the Sea of Reeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: I brought your fathers out from Egypt, and you came to the sea. The Egyptians pursued your fathers with chariots and horsemen to the Sea of Reeds.

verses.rationale: Retain third-person LORD/he within divine first-person speech and the later return to I rather than silently harmonizing speakers.
verses.before: They cried out to the LORD, and he put darkness between you and the Egyptians and brought the sea upon them and covered them. Your eyes saw what I did in Egypt. Then you lived in the wilderness many days.
verses.after: They cried out to the LORD, and he put darkness between you and the Egyptians. He brought the sea over them and covered them. Your own eyes saw what I did to Egypt. Then you lived in the wilderness for a long time.
verses.tsw_comparator: They cried out to the LORD, and he put darkness between you and the Egyptians and brought the sea upon them and covered them. Your eyes saw what I did in Egypt. Then you lived in the wilderness many days.

verses.rationale: Preserve human fighting, divine giving and destruction and resulting possession.
verses.before: I brought you into the land of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan. They fought with you, and I gave them into your hand, and you possessed their land, and I destroyed them from before you.
verses.after: I brought you to the land of the Amorites east of the Jordan. They fought against you, but I gave them into your hand. You took possession of their land, and I destroyed them before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I brought you into the land of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan. They fought with you, and I gave them into your hand, and you possessed their land, and I destroyed them from before you.

verses.rationale: Keep fought against as this account’s characterization rather than harmonizing it with another narrative.
verses.before: Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and fought against Israel. He sent and called Balaam son of Beor to curse you.
verses.after: Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, rose up and fought against Israel. He sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and fought against Israel. He sent and called Balaam son of Beor to curse you.

verses.rationale: Retain refusal, emphatic blessing and rescue hand-image without adding a psychological motive.
verses.before: Yet I was not willing to listen to Balaam, so he surely blessed you, and I rescued you from his hand.
verses.after: But I would not listen to Balaam. He blessed you instead, and I rescued you from his hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I was not willing to listen to Balaam, so he surely blessed you, and I rescued you from his hand.

verses.rationale: Keep Jericho’s people and all seven named peoples as the retrospective account presents them.
verses.before: Then you crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The lords of Jericho fought against you, and also the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Girgashite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, and I gave them into your hand.
verses.after: You crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The people of Jericho fought against you, along with the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites. I gave them into your hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The lords of Jericho fought against you, and also the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Girgashite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, and I gave them into your hand.

verses.rationale: Preserve hornet, two kings and denial of weapon agency without harmonizing the chronology or identifying the image definitively.
verses.before: I sent the hornet before you, and it drove them out from before you—the two kings of the Amorites—not by your sword and not by your bow.
verses.after: I sent the hornet ahead of you, and it drove them out before you—the two Amorite kings. It was not your sword or your bow.
verses.tsw_comparator: I sent the hornet before you, and it drove them out from before you—the two kings of the Amorites—not by your sword and not by your bow.

verses.rationale: Retain the three unearned-gift contrasts and close the divine quotation.
verses.before: I gave you a land for which you did not labor and cities that you did not build, and you live in them. You eat from vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant.”
verses.after: I gave you land you had not labored over and towns you had not built, and you settled in them. You eat from vineyards and olive trees you did not plant.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: I gave you a land for which you did not labor and cities that you did not build, and you live in them. You eat from vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant.”

verses.rationale: Keep fear, integrity, faithfulness and the repeated serve command rather than reducing it to a single act of choice.
verses.before: “Now therefore fear the LORD and serve him in integrity and in faithfulness. Put away the gods that your fathers served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the LORD.
verses.after: “Now fear the LORD and serve him with integrity and faithfulness. Put away the gods your ancestors served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Now therefore fear the LORD and serve him in integrity and in faithfulness. Put away the gods that your fathers served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retain the actual named alternatives and familiar household pledge where its wording remains clear.
verses.before: And if it is evil in your eyes to serve the LORD, choose this day whom you will serve—whether the gods your fathers served beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell. But as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.”
verses.after: If serving the LORD seems wrong to you, choose today whom you will serve: the gods your ancestors served beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites whose land you now live in. As for me and my household, we will serve the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And if it is evil in your eyes to serve the LORD, choose this day whom you will serve—whether the gods your fathers served beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell. But as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Keep the force of the reply and its contrast of allegiances.
verses.before: Then the people answered, “Far be it from us that we should forsake the LORD to serve other gods,
verses.after: The people answered, “Far be it from us to abandon the LORD and serve other gods!
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the people answered, “Far be it from us that we should forsake the LORD to serve other gods,

verses.rationale: Retain us and ancestors, slavery’s house image, visible signs and protection in both journey and human surroundings.
verses.before: for it is the LORD our God who brought us and our fathers up from the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, and who did those great signs in our sight and preserved us in all the way that we went and among all the peoples through whom we passed.
verses.after: The LORD our God is the one who brought us and our ancestors up from Egypt, from the house of slavery. He performed those great signs before our eyes and protected us along the whole way we traveled and among all the peoples we passed through.
verses.tsw_comparator: for it is the LORD our God who brought us and our fathers up from the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, and who did those great signs in our sight and preserved us in all the way that we went and among all the peoples through whom we passed.

verses.rationale: Keep the people’s comprehensive retrospective claim and resulting pledge in their voice.
verses.before: And the LORD drove out before us all the peoples, the Amorites who lived in the land. Therefore we also will serve the LORD, for he is our God.”
verses.after: The LORD drove out all the peoples before us, including the Amorites who lived in the land. We too will serve the LORD, because he is our God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD drove out before us all the peoples, the Amorites who lived in the land. Therefore we also will serve the LORD, for he is our God.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the unsettling cannot and will-not-forgive statements, without adding qualifiers to soften them.
verses.before: Yet Joshua said to the people, “You are not able to serve the LORD, for he is a holy God. He is a jealous God; he will not forgive your transgression or your sins.
verses.after: Joshua told the people, “You cannot serve the LORD, because he is a holy God, a jealous God. He will not forgive your rebellion and your sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Joshua said to the people, “You are not able to serve the LORD, for he is a holy God. He is a jealous God; he will not forgive your transgression or your sins.

verses.rationale: Keep the condition, reversal from good to harm and threatened destruction as Joshua’s warning.
verses.before: If you forsake the LORD and serve foreign gods, then he will turn and do you harm and consume you, after having done you good.”
verses.after: If you abandon the LORD and serve foreign gods, he will turn and bring harm on you and put an end to you, after doing good to you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: If you forsake the LORD and serve foreign gods, then he will turn and do you harm and consume you, after having done you good.”

verses.rationale: Retain the direct refusal of Joshua’s challenge and renewed pledge.
verses.before: And the people said to Joshua, “No, but we will serve the LORD.”
verses.after: “No!” the people told Joshua. “We will serve the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the people said to Joshua, “No, but we will serve the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Keep witnesses against themselves and their assent, distinguishing both voices.
verses.before: Then Joshua said to the people, “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the LORD, to serve him.” And they said, “We are witnesses.”
verses.after: Joshua said, “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the LORD, to serve him.” “We are witnesses,” they replied.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joshua said to the people, “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the LORD, to serve him.” And they said, “We are witnesses.”

verses.rationale: Retain gods among the present people rather than recasting them as only ancestral temptations.
verses.before: He said, “Then put away the foreign gods that are among you and incline your heart to the LORD, the God of Israel.”
verses.after: “Then put away the foreign gods among you,” he said, “and turn your hearts toward the LORD, the God of Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Then put away the foreign gods that are among you and incline your heart to the LORD, the God of Israel.”

verses.rationale: Keep service and hearing-obedience as paired commitments.
verses.before: And the people said to Joshua, “The LORD our God we will serve, and his voice we will obey.”
verses.after: The people told Joshua, “We will serve the LORD our God and obey his voice.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the people said to Joshua, “The LORD our God we will serve, and his voice we will obey.”

verses.rationale: Retain covenant and the two legal terms without inventing their content.
verses.before: So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day and set for them a statute and an ordinance at Shechem.
verses.after: That day Joshua made a covenant for the people and established a statute and an ordinance for them at Shechem.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day and set for them a statute and an ordinance at Shechem.

verses.rationale: Keep the scroll’s title distinct from Moses’ instruction in chapter 23, and retain the tree and sanctuary without relocating them.
verses.before: Joshua wrote these words in the book of the instruction of God. Then he took a great stone and set it up there under the terebinth that was by the sanctuary of the LORD.
verses.after: Joshua wrote these words in the scroll of God’s instruction. He took a large stone and set it up there beneath the terebinth in the LORD’s sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua wrote these words in the book of the instruction of God. Then he took a great stone and set it up there under the terebinth that was by the sanctuary of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserve the stone’s hearing, shift from us to you and witness language rather than replacing personification with an explanation.
verses.before: Joshua said to all the people, “Look, this stone will be a witness against us, for it has heard all the words of the LORD that he spoke with us. It will be a witness against you, lest you deny your God.”
verses.after: He told all the people, “Look, this stone will be a witness against us. It has heard all the words the LORD spoke to us. It will be a witness against you, so that you do not deny your God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua said to all the people, “Behold, this stone shall be a witness against us, for it has heard all the words of the LORD that he spoke with us. It shall be a witness against you, lest you deny your God.”

verses.rationale: Keep the distributed return and the book’s recurring inheritance term.
verses.before: Then Joshua sent the people away, each to his inheritance.
verses.after: Joshua sent the people away, each to their inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joshua sent the people away, each to his inheritance.

verses.rationale: Retain full identity, servant title and exact age.
verses.before: And it happened after these things that Joshua son of Nun, servant of the LORD, died, being one hundred ten years old.
verses.after: After these events, Joshua son of Nun, the LORD’s servant, died at the age of one hundred ten.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened after these things that Joshua son of Nun, servant of the LORD, died, being one hundred ten years old.

verses.rationale: Keep the land relationship, full place name and north-of qualifier.
verses.before: They buried him in the territory of his inheritance at Timnath-Serah, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
verses.after: They buried him within his inheritance at Timnath-serah, in Ephraim’s hill country, north of Mount Gaash.
verses.tsw_comparator: They buried him in the territory of his inheritance at Timnath-Serah, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.

verses.rationale: Preserve both generations and their knowledge as the narrator’s limit on this summary.
verses.before: Israel served the LORD all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua and who knew all the work of the LORD that he had done for Israel.
verses.after: Israel served the LORD throughout Joshua’s lifetime and throughout the lifetimes of the elders who outlived him and knew all the LORD had done for Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Israel served the LORD all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua and who knew all the work of the LORD that he had done for Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep the bones’ journey, purchased plot, full seller relationship and untranslated uncertain money unit.
verses.before: The bones of Joseph, which the sons of Israel had brought up from Egypt, they buried at Shechem in the portion of the field that Jacob had bought from the sons of Hamor, father of Shechem, for one hundred qesitah. It became an inheritance for the sons of Joseph.
verses.after: The Israelites buried Joseph’s bones, which they had brought up from Egypt, at Shechem, in the plot Jacob had bought from the sons of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for one hundred qesitahs. It became an inheritance for Joseph’s descendants.
verses.tsw_comparator: The bones of Joseph, which the sons of Israel had brought up from Egypt, they buried at Shechem in the portion of the field that Jacob had bought from the sons of Hamor, father of Shechem, for one hundred qesitah. It became an inheritance for the sons of Joseph.

verses.rationale: Preserve lineage and grant to the son while retaining the hill-name’s geographical and personal senses.
verses.before: Eleazar son of Aaron died, and they buried him at Gibeah of Phinehas his son, which had been given to him in the hill country of Ephraim.
verses.after: Eleazar son of Aaron also died. They buried him at Gibeath-phinehas, the hill given to his son Phinehas in Ephraim’s hill country.
verses.tsw_comparator: Eleazar son of Aaron died, and they buried him at Gibeah of Phinehas his son, which had been given to him in the hill country of Ephraim.
